title: Inference queue resilience — customer credit offer & status update (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing draft combining: (A) a concise status-page update series for public posting, (B) a customer post-incident summary with technical context, and (C) a proposed goodwill package (credits + optional replay assistance). Intended recipients: customers impacted by inference request queue jitter and elevated tail latency on 2029-06-09 through 2029-06-11.

One-line summary (for execs / top of page):
On 2029-06-09 we observed intermittent high tail latency and delayed request dequeuing for a subset of hosted API tenants caused by an autoscaler race that triggered excessive KV-cache evictions. We mitigated the issue, restored normal throughput, and are offering targeted credits plus optional replay support for impacted tenants.

Impact (customer-facing):
- Window: 2029-06-09 02:14 UTC -> 2029-06-11 08:02 UTC (intermittent reoccurrence nights UTC).
- Observable effects: increased per-request latency spikes (p50 normal, p95/p99 elevated), streaming sessions occasionally paused/rebuffered, and a small number of requests failed with 503 while retries were in flight.
- Scope: ~2.6% of hosted API requests across multiple regions; concentrated on tenants with high short-burst concurrency using short-context chat sessions with heavy prefix reuse.
- Data integrity: No customer data was exfiltrated or modified. All persisted artifacts (logs, embeddings) verified intact.

Technical summary (high level, for customers who want details):
- What happened: A timing interaction between the autoscaler (scale-down/scale-up throttles) and the runtime’s KV-cache eviction policy produced transient cache thinning during scale operations. When a node scaled down and the router redirected new requests to warming nodes, a sequence of cache evictions caused increased cold-KV lookups and longer per-token kernel selection time. In high-burst paths this manifested as request queuing jitter and occasional upstream timeouts.
- Root cause: race between autoscaler lifecycle events and cache replication/rehydration; eviction triggers were too aggressive during rapid scaling bursts.
- Why it affected some customers more: tenants with frequent short-lived chat sessions rely heavily on prefix/KV reuse. Those workloads are more sensitive to transient cache misses.
- Confirmed fixes applied: immediate throttle on scale-down actions (reduces churn), temporary increase in KV-cache retention for warm nodes, and a runtime patch to avoid synchronous eviction during node admission.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2029-06-09 02:14 — First spike detected by alerting: p99 > target in us-west-2.
- 2029-06-09 02:19 — Triage started: SRE + Serving Runtime + Customer Success on call.
- 2029-06-09 02:40 — Short-term mitigation: raised scale-down cooldowns and increased cache retention threshold. Noticeable reduction in spike frequency.
- 2029-06-09 03:30 — Rolling configuration bump deployed across active pools. Monitoring showed p99 trending down.
- 2029-06-10 01:12 — Small reoccurrence aligned with a regional autoscaler job; further patch applied to runtime to stop synchronous eviction during node hand-off.
- 2029-06-11 08:02 — Final verification: metrics stable across regions for 24 hours; clinical validation with test traffic and a set of customer-supplied prompt traces.

Mitigations and customer actions (what we did and what customers may want to do):
- We did: (1) applied emergency config change to autoscaler cooldowns, (2) increased in-memory KV retention and warmed caches proactively during load windows, (3) rolled a runtime patch that defers bulk eviction to background workers, (4) executed targeted replays to validate recovery, (5) implemented monitoring rule adjustments to catch the autoscaler-cache interaction earlier.
- Recommended customer-side mitigations (optional):
  - For customers with many short-lived chat sessions: consider enabling short-term sticky routing to warm nodes (config flag we can activate for you).
  - If you observed unexplained client-side timeouts, please share a representative trace (timestamps + request ids) so we can correlate and offer a targeted replay.

Goodwill offer (proposed language for CS to send):
- Redwood will automatically apply a usage credit equal to 5% of billed hosted inference charges for the affected billing cycle for tenants who had >= 0.5% of their requests impacted during the incident window.
- For enterprise tenants with contractual SLAs, we will initiate an SLA exception review and, where appropriate, additional credits per the SLA terms.
- Optional hands-on replay assistance: our Solutions Engineering team can accept a limited set of customer traces and run a replay in a private staging pool to validate outputs and provide remediation suggestions. Please opt-in by replying to this message or opening INC-4527.

Status page update snippets (short, to be posted sequentially):
1) Initial: "Investigating increased request latency in multiple regions affecting a small subset of hosted API requests. Engineers are triaging. (2029-06-09 02:20 UTC)"
2) Mitigating: "Mitigations in flight — autoscaler scale-down cooldowns increased and cache retention raised. Expect reduced frequency of spikes; working on a code fix. (2029-06-09 03:00 UTC)"
3) Partial resolution: "Partial resolution observed; continuing to monitor. Targeted runtime patch queued for rolling deploy. (2029-06-10 01:30 UTC)"
4) Resolved: "Issue resolved. Metrics stable for 24h; credit offer and optional replay assistance being coordinated with impacted customers. (2029-06-11 08:10 UTC)"

Customer Q&A (for CS agents to copy/paste):
Q: Will I get an automatic credit?
A: If your tenant saw >= 0.5% of requests impacted during the window, you will receive an automatic credit equal to 5% of your hosted inference charges for the affected billing period. If you believe you were impacted but not captured by our telemetry, reply with example request ids and timestamps and we will review.

Q: Did any model outputs change or get lost?
A: No persistent data loss or corruption was detected. Some in-flight requests experienced retries or timed out; we can help replay those traces to verify outputs.

Q: Are you changing the autoscaler permanently?
A: Permanent changes will be phased in after validation. Immediate changes were conservative: longer cooldowns and higher cache retention. The runtime patch to defer eviction will be promoted after additional canaries and load testing.

Draft approvals needed:
- CS lead (Aisha) review for tone and credit language.
- Legal to confirm credit wording for enterprise contracts (Kiran).
- Engineering sign-off on the technical blurb (Diego + Maya).

Next steps (internal):
- Finalize customer list by 2029-06-16 and send outbound notices 2029-06-17.
- Complete postmortem doc with deep dive and permanent remediation plan by 2029-06-25.
- Track credit application in billing system and confirm with each tenant within 7 days of notice.

Draft message for impacted customers (email/message body — direct use):
Subject: Redwood update: short-lived latency spikes and credit offer

Hi [Customer name],

We want to make you aware of a recent service disruption that affected a small portion of requests to Redwood’s hosted inference. Between 2029-06-09 and 2029-06-11 we observed intermittent elevated tail latency and a small number of timeouts caused by a timing interaction between autoscaling and our runtime cache eviction. We’ve implemented mitigations and a runtime patch; metrics have been stable for 24 hours.

As a gesture of goodwill we will apply a usage credit equal to 5% of your hosted inference charges for the impacted billing cycle if your tenant experienced measurable impact (we’ll identify those automatically). If you’d like us to replay any specific request traces or want short-term sticky routing enabled for your tenant, reply to this message or open INC-4527 and we’ll prioritize assistance.

We appreciate your patience and will follow up with a link to the full post-incident report when it’s published.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Notes / open questions: 
- Confirm precise credit percentage with Finance/legal if enterprise contract terms require bespoke adjustments.
- Determine whether to expand the auto-credit threshold from 0.5% to 0.25% for high-value tenants (requires Finance ok).
- Validate statuspage snippet wording with comms team to ensure consistent public messaging.

-- end of draft --
